h1: The 7 Best Video Doorbells That Work With Mechanical Chimes of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Doorbells for Mechanical Chimes: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 video doorbells compared on wiring, power type and resolution, with notes on which suit a ding-dong chime inside your home.
summary: The Ring Wired Doorbell 2K Plus is the sensible default: it runs from existing doorbell wiring, so it is the type of device that can still trigger the chime in your hall. The Ring Wired 4K Pro is the sharper upgrade. The WYZE Wired v2 is the cheapest way in, and the Blink Wired 2K+ suits an Alexa home. Battery models like the Ring Battery 2K and eufy E340 are easier to install but are not wired into your old chime.
intro: A mechanical chime is the little box in your hall with a solenoid and two tone bars. It rings because the old doorbell button completes a low-voltage circuit. A video doorbell has to sit in that same circuit if you want the ding-dong to survive the upgrade, which is why the first question is how a doorbell is powered, not how sharp its picture is.

Seven models are covered here. Most of the strong picks are wired, because wiring into the existing doorbell circuit is the usual route to keep a mechanical chime. Battery and PoE models are included for homes without suitable wiring, but they come with caveats you should read before you buy.

products.name: Ring Wired Doorbell 2K Plus
products.verdict: Wired power, 2K video and no battery to recharge. The easiest fit for a house with a working chime.
products.description:
Ring's 2K Plus is a wired model that uses your existing doorbell wiring rather than a battery. That matters for chimes: it is the same style of connection a mechanical chime expects. It records in 2K, enough for faces and packages at a normal porch distance.

It ranks above the 4K Pro for most buyers because the extra resolution does not change whether the chime works, and a lower price helps. It also ranks above the Wyze because Ring's app and ecosystem are broader. Check that your doorbell transformer matches the voltage on the listing before you order.

It suits a household that wants a no-fuss upgrade without moving the chime.
products.idealFor: Homes with a working mechanical chime.
products.skipIf: You rent and cannot touch the wiring.

products.name: Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro
products.verdict: 4K video and up to 10x zoom on the same wired platform. Worth it if you want detail.
products.description:
The 4K Pro records in 4K and offers up to 10x zoom, so you can read a delivery label from the step. It uses the same wired approach as the 2K Plus, which keeps it in line with a mechanical chime setup.

It ranks second because a mechanical chime does not care about resolution. If your main reason for choosing a doorbell is that chime, the cheaper 2K Plus does the same job. The 4K Pro is the pick when your porch is wide, your driveway is long or you want to check details at distance.

Good for a larger entry where the sharper image will be used.

products.name: WYZE Wired Doorbell Camera v2
products.verdict: Head-to-toe view, starlight night color and an accessible price for a wired 2K doorbell.
products.description:
Wyze's v2 is a wired 2K doorbell with a wide view that shows a visitor from head to toe, plus a starlight sensor that keeps night footage in color rather than grey. It is compact enough to fit on a narrow door frame.

It is cheaper than the Ring wired models, which is why it ranks third. The compromise is a smaller ecosystem, and you should check the listing for how it works with an existing mechanical chime before buying, because chime support varies by model.

A solid starter for a budget-minded household that likes the head-to-toe view.
products.idealFor: Budget upgrades with a wide view.
products.skipIf: You want the broadest smart-home support.

products.name: Blink Wired Doorbell 2K+
products.verdict: Connects to existing doorbell wiring and delivers 2K video inside the Amazon ecosystem.
products.description:
Blink's wired 2K+ connects to your existing doorbell wiring and records in 2K. It belongs to Amazon's family of devices, so it fits easily into an Alexa home alongside Echo displays and speakers.

It ranks below the Ring models because Ring's app, accessories and features are more mature, and below the Wyze for the price gap only in the Wyze's favor. Blink's strength is simplicity: a basic, wired doorbell that does the core job.

A fit for an Alexa household that wants a wired doorbell without extra complexity.
products.idealFor: Alexa households with wiring in place.
products.skipIf: You use Google Home or Apple Home.

products.name: Ring Battery Doorbell 2K
products.verdict: Battery power means no wiring, but it will not ring a hall mechanical chime on its own.
products.description:
The Ring Battery Doorbell 2K runs on a battery, so there is nothing to wire. It records 2K video with a wide-angle lens and up to 6x zoom, and lets you see, hear and speak in real time.

It ranks fifth because the point of this guide is a mechanical chime, and a battery doorbell is not connected to your doorbell circuit. You will usually need a separate chime accessory to hear it inside. For apartments and renters who cannot touch wiring, though, nothing else here is as simple to install.

Best for renters and for doors with no existing doorbell wiring.
cons: Does not use the old chime
products.idealFor: Renters and doors with no wiring.
products.skipIf: You want your hall chime to ring.

products.name: eufy Security Video Doorbell E340
products.verdict: Two cameras, one for visitors and one for the doorstep, with battery power and no wiring.
products.description:
The E340 carries two cameras: one for the visitor and one aimed down at packages on the doorstep. It is battery powered, so installation needs no new wiring, and it records in 2K.

It ranks sixth for the same reason as the Ring Battery: a battery doorbell is not connected to your doorbell circuit, so a mechanical chime will not ring from it directly. The dual camera design is the real reason to buy, and it helps if parcels are your main worry.

Good for homes with package theft concerns and no usable wiring.
cons: Does not trigger the old chime

products.name: REOLINK Video Doorbell PoE 2K
products.verdict: A PoE doorbell with a 135-degree view, for homes with an ethernet cable at the door.
products.description:
Reolink's PoE doorbell takes its power and data over a single ethernet cable, so there is no battery to recharge. It records 2K video with a 135-degree field of view and ships with a wedge kit for doors that are not vertical.

It ranks last because PoE is not the same connection as the low-voltage wiring behind a mechanical chime. Unless you already have an ethernet run at the door, installation is a bigger job than any other model here, and the chime question is the one to check on the listing.

A niche pick for a tech-comfortable owner with a PoE network and an ethernet cable at the door.
products.idealFor: PoE networks with a cable at the door.
products.skipIf: You only have old doorbell wiring.

whatMatters.detail: A mechanical chime runs on a small transformer, often 16 to 24 volts. Most wired video doorbells list a supported voltage range, and one below it will not power the camera reliably. Read the transformer's label or the chime's rating and compare it with the doorbell listing.

A battery doorbell has no connection to the doorbell circuit, so it cannot ring a mechanical chime directly. You usually use a plug-in chime or the phone app. If you love the ding-dong sound, choose a wired model.

Some video doorbells need a small bypass or power kit installed across the chime so the circuit keeps flowing. The kit sits inside the chime box, and the listing or the manual explains whether you need one. Do not skip it, because it prevents buzzing.
2K is plenty for a small porch. 4K and 10x zoom help on wide porches and long driveways, where a face is far from the lens. Pick resolution based on the distance, not on the box number alone.
Live view is often free, but saved clips and history usually need a monthly plan. Check which features are free on the listing, and decide whether you want cloud storage before you choose a brand.

howToChoose.intro: Start with what is behind the door.

cards.label: Wired
cards.text: Connects to doorbell wiring, so it can work with a mechanical chime and needs no recharging. Picks: Ring Wired 2K Plus, Ring Wired 4K Pro, WYZE Wired v2, Blink Wired 2K+.

cards.label: Battery
cards.text: No wiring, quick to install, but it does not ring a hall chime directly and needs recharging. Picks: Ring Battery 2K, eufy E340.

howToChoose.note: If the mechanical chime matters, go wired. Choose battery only when wiring is not an option.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A tall field of view or a second camera that sees the doorstep, plus color night footage.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The eufy E340, whose second camera is aimed at parcels, or the WYZE Wired v2, whose head-to-toe view also shows the doorstep.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a long driveway or a wide porch. The Ring Wired 4K Pro shows detail at distance that 2K cannot.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: A standard porch and a working chime are enough. The WYZE Wired v2 covers the basics for less.

faq.q: Will a video doorbell ring my existing chime?
faq.a: Wired models that connect to your doorbell circuit usually can. Battery models generally cannot. Check each listing and confirm your transformer voltage first.

faq.q: Do I need a bypass kit?
faq.a: Some wired doorbells need a small power kit installed across the chime to prevent buzzing or loss of power. The listing and manual say whether yours is required.

faq.q: Can I use a battery doorbell with a mechanical chime?
faq.a: Not directly. A battery doorbell is not connected to the doorbell circuit, so you would use a separate plug-in chime. The Ring Battery 2K and eufy E340 follow this model.

faq.q: Is the Ring Wired 4K Pro worth it over the 2K Plus?
faq.a: If you want to see detail at a distance, yes. The 4K Pro has 4K video and up to 10x zoom. For ordinary porches, the 2K Plus is enough and costs less.
Many wired doorbells list a supported range, often 16 to 24 volts AC. Read the label on your transformer or chime and compare it with the doorbell listing.

faq.q: Does PoE work with a mechanical chime?
faq.a: PoE uses an ethernet cable rather than the doorbell circuit, so check the listing before assuming it will ring a mechanical chime. The Reolink PoE model is the one for homes with ethernet at the door.

finalTake: For most homes with a working chime, the Ring Wired Doorbell 2K Plus is the safe choice, since it plugs into the same kind of wiring your chime already uses. Pay up for the Ring Wired 4K Pro only if you want detail at distance. The WYZE Wired v2 is the cheaper route, and the Blink Wired 2K+ suits Alexa homes. Choose a battery model like the Ring Battery 2K only when you cannot wire it, and expect it not to ring the old chime.
